newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia confident on wheat sales to India - AWB.
newsitem.headline: Australia confident on wheat sales to India - AWB.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) was confident it would complete its one million tonne wheat shipment to India this year despite problems raised about weed seed content, an AWB spokesman said.
The spokesman was commenting to Reuters after a delegation of Indian officials visited Australia last week to discuss shipping, quality assurance and weed seed content.
The weed seed issue was now with the Indian side with the AWB waiting for its reply, he said.
"We're confident that we will meet the one million tonne shipment and that we can easily meet their requirements, being clean and green," he said.

A report in the Sydney Morning Herald on Thursday, sourced from New Delhi, said the fate of a A$200 million sale of Australian wheat to India was in doubt after Indian complaints about the quality of previous shipments.
The AWB official denied that this was so.
AWB officials also said that an AWB delegation to India had not been postponed because Indian officials were preparing a report into the delegation's visit to Australia.
Relevant AWB officials were in London for International Grains Council meetings, they said.
The AWB official said on Thursday that suggestions that India and Australia were in a stand-off over the weed seed complaints were not accurate.
The weed seed problem involves export contracts covering India's purchase of 2.325 million tonnes of Australian wheat.
Of the total, 1.3 million tonnes have been shipped, with the rest due for shipment after July.
Indian officials complained about the presence of weed seed in the wheat after first shipments were received.
